interest: Japanese training squadron's 1933 goodwill visit to Vancouver.
overview: This file comprises records from April 1933 documenting the goodwill visit of the Imperial Japanese Navy's Training Squadron, consisting of the cruisers Yakumo and Iwate under the command of Vice Admiral Gengo Hyakutake, to Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The file contains a Department of State cross-reference sheet (Document File Note) referencing Despatch No. 1382 and the four-page consular despatch dated April 11, 1933, prepared by American Consul General Ely E. Palmer in Vancouver. The despatch describes the squadron's arrival on April 5 following official calls at Victoria, Vice Admiral Hyakutake's public statement emphasizing Pacific peace and goodwill, a municipal banquet hosted by the Mayor and City Council of Vancouver, a reception hosted by the acting Japanese Consul, and shipboard visits by Canadian dignitaries and the public. It also details diplomatic and naval communication with the U.S. Navy's Thirteenth Naval District in Seattle regarding the squadron's departure for San Francisco, and incorporates local press reaction, notably an editorial from the Vancouver Sun expressing friendship with the Japanese people while noting disapproval of Japan's policies in Manchukuo.
